newsitem.title: USA: MUNI BUYSIDE - Cooner says redemption cash to munis.
newsitem.headline: MUNI BUYSIDE - Cooner says redemption cash to munis.

text.p: Roughly $66 billion of redemption money is expected to flow back to municipal bond investors in June and July, and James Cooner, head of the Bank of New York's tax-exempt bond management division, believes munis will recapture most of it.

"Municipal money seeks tax exemption and income as opposed to the possibilities of future capital appreciation, which is the money that goes into the stock market," said Cooner, a senior vice president at the bank. "So I would think that a pretty good percentage of that money would tend to gravitate back into munis."
In addition, equities' allure has faded in recent days and weeks, given that market's "roller coaster" performance, Cooner said.
"People are maybe not as enthralled with a stock market that can go up and down 500 points," he said.

An investor in today's municipal market can go out to the 10-year range and get a 5.50 percent tax-free yield, Cooner said. By comparison, an investor buying a stock as represented by the Standard & Poor's 500 would get approximately a two percent dividend yield that he or she would be taxed on.

If the investor is in a high tax bracket and located in an area with big state taxes as well, he or she would occupy a close to a 50 percent tax bracket, Cooner said. That would whittle the 2.0 percent dividend yield down to 1.0 percent, he said.
"Well, I can go out and get five times that tax-free from a municipal bond," Cooner said.
